name: Zygomatic reduction
lead: Zygomatic reduction, also called malarplasty, cheekbone reduction or cheekbone shaving, is a surgical procedure intended to narrow or lower the projection of the cheekbones (the zygomatic bones). The zygomatic bone forms the cheekbone and part of the eye socket wall [1].

The procedure is discussed in looksmaxxing forums mainly by people with wide faces, with participants disagreeing about whether width comes from bone or fat and whether the surgery improves or harms facial proportions [2]. The material available for this entry is limited to a general anatomy reference and forum discussion.

paras: The zygomatic bone is a paired bone at the upper outer part of the face. It forms part of the lateral wall and floor of the orbit and articulates with the frontal, sphenoid, temporal and maxillary bones [1]. Wikipedia notes that prominent cheekbones are considered attractive in some cultures and that some people undergo cheek augmentation, the opposite operation; it does not discuss cheekbone reduction [1].

lore.intro: A looksmax.org thread on cheekbone reduction shows the practice discussed as an option for wide faces, with disagreement about who benefits [2].

claims.claim: A wide face may come from bone rather than fat, and cheekbone reduction can improve it.
claims.believers: The original poster says a wide face is due to fat or bone, that buccal fat removal can look aged and unnatural, that people of Asian descent tend to have wide cheekbones, and that malarplasty can go very well or very badly, with before-and-after examples posted [2].
claims.experts: No published studies in the sources reviewed here evaluate cheekbone reduction outcomes.

claims.claim: Cheekbone shaving mainly reduces forward projection, not width.
claims.believers: The poster says shaving primarily reduces forward projection rather than width, and that width is what most people want to change [2].
claims.experts: No published studies in the sources reviewed here address this.

claims.claim: Surgery should only be done when the proportions truly call for it, since it can ruin a harmonious face.
claims.believers: Replies say the surgery suits a person whose face is wide with a disproportionate jaw, but not a person whose bone structure is already ideal and who lacks forward growth; they cite a widely discussed case of a man who had cheek and jaw reduction as an example of a result they considered a loss [2].
claims.experts: No published studies in the sources reviewed here evaluate how patient selection affects outcome.

card.summary: Surgery to narrow or flatten the cheekbones; popular in Asian aesthetic surgery, with no outcome studies in the wiki's sources.
card.note: Forum members themselves report mixed before-and-after outcomes; no studies found.

quick.overview:
Zygomatic reduction is a surgery that reshapes or repositions the cheekbones to make the face narrower. It is also called malarplasty or cheekbone shaving.

On looksmax.org, users with wide faces discuss it and argue over whether it helps or ruins proportions. No studies were found for this wiki entry.
quick.mechanism: The bone of the cheek is cut and reshaped or repositioned inward, as forum posters describe it. Some say shaving mainly reduces forward projection rather than width.
quick.risks: Forum users describe results ranging from very good to very bad. It is a bone-cutting operation under anaesthesia; no complication data were available in the sources used here.
